subject: Mixing Lines and points and using the legend

messages.author: e7a71d967e60bb41
messages.subject: Mixing Lines and points and using the legend
parts:
Dear All,
Have a look at the code snippet at the end of the email.
I may simplify it if needed (I have just taken it almost as it was for a
figure I want to include in a paper, so it also uses the package
tikzDevice to include latex expressions in the figure).
I generate a two plots; the second plot is the same as the first one but
an extra point (the dataset I label Filippov has been added).
Now, overall I have 5 datasets;
(1) Collision rate should be plotted as points
(2-3-4-)collision rate fit, Vainstein et al, Dahneke should be lines
with different line styles,
(5) Filippov should be a single point and appear as such in the legend

Well, no matter what I have tried, I cannot get the job done (i.e. I
played with
scale_shape_manual("", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values=c(1))
and tried values like c(1,0,0,0,2) but it does not do what I would like
(i.e. no symbols for datasets 2 to 4 (which are plotted with a line) but
a point for dataset 5.
I suspect I must be making a trivial error, but any help is appreciated.
Cheers

Lorenzo


#######################################################################à

library(ggplot2)
library(tikzDevice)


x<-seq(0,1,by=0.1)

ml_rew <- as.data.frame(cbind(x, exp(-x)))

names(ml_rew) <- c("k","beta")

ml <- as.data.frame(cbind(x, exp(-2*x)))


names(ml) <- c("k","beta")


ml2 <- as.data.frame(cbind(x,exp(-3*x)))


names(ml2) <- c("k","beta")


ml4 <- as.data.frame(cbind(x, exp(-4*x)))
names(ml4) <- c("k", "beta")


ml5 <- as.data.frame(t(cbind(c(0.5,0.5))))
names(ml5) <- c("k", "beta")


ml_tmp <- rbind(transform(ml_rew, set="Collision rate"),
transform(ml, set="Collision rate fit"), transform(ml2,
set="Vainstein {\\it et al.}")
,transform(ml4, set="Dahneke"))


lbls <- levels(ml_tmp$set)

gpl2 <- ggplot(ml_tmp, aes(x=k, y=beta, colour=set,
shape=set,linetype=set)) +


geom_point(size=4.) +
geom_point(size=3.8) +
geom_point(size=3.6) +

geom_line(size=1.5) +
opts( panel.background=theme_rect(fill='white', size=1.5))+


scale_shape_manual("", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values=c(1)) +
scale_colour_manual("", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values=c(1,2,3,4)) +
scale_linetype_manual("", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values=c(0,1,2,4)) +

xlab(expression(paste("$k$")))+
ylab(expression(paste("$\\beta_k^{\\perp}/\\beta_1$")))+


scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,1), breaks=seq(0,1,by=0.1))+
scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0.,1), breaks=seq(0.,1,by=0.1))+
geom_text(aes(y=0.7,x=60,label="(b)", angle=0), size=10,
col="black")+


opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 22, colour="black"))+
opts(legend.text = theme_text(size = 14, vjust=0.4))+
opts(legend.title = theme_text(size = 18,hjust=0))+
opts(legend.position = c(0.75, 0.8),
legend.background=theme_rect(col=0),
legend.key = theme_rect(colour = NA))+
opts(panel.grid.minor = theme_blank())+
opts(axis.ticks = theme_segment(colour = "black",
size=1),axis.ticks.length = unit(0.15, "cm"))+
opts(panel.grid.major = theme_blank())+
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 22, angle=90))+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=18, colour="black",vjust=1))+
opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size=18, colour="black", hjust=1))

tikz('test.tex', standAlone = TRUE, width=5,height=5)
print(gpl2)
dev.off()

tools::texi2dvi('test.tex',pdf=T)

#Now try a second plot.


ml_tmp <- rbind(transform(ml_rew, set="Collision rate"),
transform(ml, set="Collision rate fit"), transform(ml2,
set="Vainstein {\\it et al.}")
,transform(ml4, set="Dahneke"),transform(ml5,
set="Filippov"))

lbls <- levels(ml_tmp$set)

gpl2 <- ggplot(ml_tmp, aes(x=k, y=beta, colour=set,
shape=set,linetype=set)) +

#ggplot(ml_tmp, aes(x=l, y=one_two_separate, colour=set, shape=set,
fill=set)) +

geom_point(size=4.) +
geom_point(size=3.8) +
geom_point(size=3.6) +

geom_line(size=1.5) +
opts( panel.background=theme_rect(fill='white', size=1.5))+


scale_shape_manual("", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values=c(1)) +
scale_colour_manual("", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values=c(1,2,3,4,5)) +
scale_linetype_manual("", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls,values=c(0,1,2,4,0))+


#extra stuff
xlab(expression(paste("$k$")))+
ylab(expression(paste("$\\beta_k^{\\perp}/\\beta_1$")))+


scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,1), breaks=seq(0,1,by=0.1))+
scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0.,1), breaks=seq(0.,1,by=0.1))+
geom_text(aes(y=0.7,x=60,label="(b)", angle=0), size=10,
col="black")+


opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 22, colour="black"))+
opts(legend.text = theme_text(size = 14, vjust=0.4))+
opts(legend.title = theme_text(size = 18,hjust=0))+
opts(legend.position = c(0.75, 0.8),
legend.background=theme_rect(col=0),
legend.key = theme_rect(colour = NA))+
opts(panel.grid.minor = theme_blank())+
opts(axis.ticks = theme_segment(colour = "black",
size=1),axis.ticks.length = unit(0.15, "cm"))+
opts(panel.grid.major = theme_blank())+
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 22, angle=90))+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=18, colour="black",vjust=1))+
opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size=18, colour="black", hjust=1))

tikz('test2.tex', standAlone = TRUE, width=5,height=5)
print(gpl2)
dev.off()

tools::texi2dvi('test2.tex',pdf=T)

messages.subject: Re: Mixing Lines and points and using the legend
parts:
On Sun, 2010-06-20 at 20:04 -0500, Hadley Wickham wrote:
> Hi Lorenzo,
>
> Could you try making a simpler example? I think it may be a legend
> bug where legends don't correctly report what data they are related
> too.
>
> Hadley

Hi Hadley,
Apologies for the delay but I have been unwell.
I think I sorted out my problems: I plot the different datasets with
both lines and points; I then suppress the lines when plotting certain
datasets with by setting =0 their line type and the points of other
datasets by setting =NA their shape.
See the snippet at the end of the email.
Cheers

Lorenzo

###################################################################àà


library(ggplot2)

x<-seq(0,1,by=0.1)

ml_rew <- as.data.frame(cbind(x, exp(-x)))
#ml_rew <- as.data.frame(cbind(seq(dim(ml_rew)[1]),ml_rew))

ml_tmp <- rbind(transform(ml_rew, set="Collision rate"),
transform(ml, set="Collision rate fit"), transform(ml2,

scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,1), breaks=seq(0,1,by=0.1))+
scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0.,1), breaks=seq(0.,1,by=0.1))+
geom_text(aes(y=0.7,x=60,label="(b)", angle=0), size=10,
col="black")+
opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 22, colour="black"))+
opts(legend.text = theme_text(size = 14, vjust=0.4))+
opts(legend.title = theme_text(size = 18,hjust=0))+
opts(legend.position = c(0.75, 0.8),
legend.background=theme_rect(col=0),
legend.key = theme_rect(colour = NA))+
opts(panel.grid.minor = theme_blank())+
opts(axis.ticks = theme_segment(colour = "black",
size=1),axis.ticks.length = unit(0.15, "cm"))+
opts(panel.grid.major = theme_blank())+
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 22, angle=90))+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=18, colour="black",vjust=1))+
opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size=18, colour="black", hjust=1))
